claude.rationale: This was a whole-company, all-cash reverse triangular merger in which the entire corporate entity — target plus all utility subsidiaries (Indiana Gas, SIGECO, VEDO via VUHI) — became a wholly owned subsidiary of CenterPoint, so the customer-facing utility products (T4) and the operational processes/utilities that produce and deliver them (T5) crossed the ownership boundary together as an intact going concern, not as a carved-out asset separated from its operations — hence gap_45=0. The Employee Matters provisions bound the acquirer to two years of same/better responsibilities, comparable pay/benefits, honored union contracts, and multi-year Evansville headquarters/operational-support commitments, so the people/organization (T6) transferred coherently alongside the processes (T5) — hence gap_56=0. Controlling intent was coded replace because the target's entire board and management ceased serving and CenterPoint's designee Prochazka became sole director at the effective time.

grok.rationale: The deal was a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which Vectren survived as a wholly owned CenterPoint subsidiary and its utilities, nonutility businesses, and intermediate holding company VUHI all crossed intact (8-K Item 2.01; DEFM14A Proposed Merger), so customer-facing utility products/services (T4) and the operational processes that deliver them (T5) moved together with no structural product-vs-process carve-out at closing. Employee Matters commitments bound CenterPoint for two years to same-or-better roles, pay, benefits, location continuity, and honor of union contracts for Company employees, and headquarters/key operational activities were contractually retained in Evansville, so processes (T5) and the organization that runs them (T6) likewise transferred coherently together; no transitional-services gap was required or documented.

openai.rationale: The entire Vectren entity and its subsidiaries, including its utility businesses, crossed the ownership boundary, while CenterPoint committed to retain key operational activities and utility-support functions in Evansville; therefore, no product-versus-process mismatch is documented at closing. Operational processes moved with the workforce under two-year responsibility, location, compensation, benefit, severance, and union-contract protections, although Vectren and VUHI's directors ceased serving and were replaced by the acquirer's designee; this does not document a process-versus-organization gap at closing.
